home.headline: Real testers for your open-source project
home.lead: Crashscouts connects developers with volunteer testers. Publish a test campaign with clear tasks, let people try your software and get structured feedback you can act on.
home.facts: Free and open source (AGPL) · No tracking, no ads · Small projects are found too
home.step1Text: Describe what to test, on which platforms, and how many testers you need. Add test tasks so people know where to start.
home.step2Text: Volunteers find your campaign on Discover, join and work through the tasks at their own pace.
home.step3Text: Bug reports and suggestions arrive in one inbox, with steps to reproduce, expected and actual result, and the environment. You decide what to fix.
home.campaignsEmptyTitle: The first campaigns are on their way
home.campaignsEmptyText: No public test campaign is open right now. Meanwhile you can browse the projects on Discover.
home.why1Text: The platform itself is AGPL licensed; you can read, run and improve every line.
home.why2Text: No analytics scripts, no ads, no cookie banner. Statistics are counted on the server, never per person.
home.why3Text: Discover sorts by recent activity, never by popularity, so a new project is found as easily as a known one.
home.welcomeText: Start a project to find testers, or join a campaign and help someone else ship better software.

publish.proposedText: Only the text becomes public – never screenshots or logs, and not your name. You can make it private again at any time.
publish.publicNotice: This feedback is public: everyone who can see the campaign can read the text.

attachments.title: Screenshots and logs
attachments.intro: Only the project team and you see these files. PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 5 MB; TXT, LOG or JSON up to 2 MB; at most 5 files.

problem.not_participant: Only testers who take part in this campaign can give feedback.
problem.campaign_closed: This campaign no longer takes feedback.
problem.blocked: Moderators blocked this content; it cannot be changed.
problem.not_author: Only the author can do this.
problem.feedback_locked: The team already looked at this feedback, so it can no longer be changed.
problem.invalid_status: This status change is not possible.
problem.invalid_duplicate: Choose another feedback of this campaign.
problem.not_proposed: The team has not proposed to publish this feedback.
problem.invalid_file: Upload a PNG, JPEG or WebP image of at most 5 MB, or a UTF-8 TXT, LOG or JSON file of at most 2 MB.
problem.too_many_attachments: A feedback can have at most 5 files.
problem.rateLimited: You sent a lot in a short time. Try again later.
problem.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

errors.title: Enter a title of at most 120 characters.
errors.platform: Choose your operating system or device.
errors.task: Choose a task of this campaign.

inbox.title: Feedback inbox
inbox.intro: All feedback of this campaign. Only your team sees who wrote it and the attached files.
inbox.newCount_one: {{count}} new feedback is waiting for your team.
inbox.newCount_other: {{count}} new feedback are waiting for your team.

manage.title: Handle this feedback
manage.authorTold: The author gets a short email about the new status.
manage.proposeText: Only the text becomes public, after the author agrees – never files or the author's name.
manage.waiting: Waiting for the author's consent to make it public.

discover.title: Discover
discover.intro: Find open-source projects and public test campaigns. Sorted by recent activity, never by popularity, so small projects are found too.
discover.searchHint: Every word must match; the beginning of a word is enough.
discover.hasCampaign: Only projects with an open test campaign
discover.noProjectsText: Try fewer filters or other words. Projects that are not open source appear when you choose “All licences”.
discover.campaignsLocked: Public test campaigns are not open yet. They appear here once the platform opens them.

suspension.banner: Your account is suspended: you can read, but not create, change or report anything.
suspension.title: Your account is suspended
suspension.permanent: Permanently, unless an appeal is accepted.
suspension.effect: You can sign in, read, export your data, change your password and two-factor methods and delete your account. You cannot create, change, report, give feedback, join or invite, and your profile is hidden from others.
suspension.appealHint: Explain why the suspension is a mistake. You can appeal once; at most 1,000 characters.
suspension.appeal_sent: Your appeal was sent. The moderators will decide.
suspension.appeal_failed: The appeal could not be sent.
suspension.refused: This is not possible while your account is suspended.

appealState.pending: Your appeal is waiting for the moderators' decision.
appealState.upheld: The moderators reviewed your appeal and kept the suspension.

moderation.title: Suspension
moderation.accept: Accept appeal and lift the suspension
moderation.messageHint: The person sees this message with the reason and the end. Reporters only learn that their report was reviewed.
moderation.endsOnHint: The suspension ends at the end of this day (UTC). Leave empty for a permanent suspension and tick the box below.
moderation.permanent: Permanently (until an appeal is accepted or a moderator lifts it)
moderation.confirm: Suspend this account: read only, hidden profile; the person is emailed and can appeal once.
moderation.cannot: This account cannot be suspended here: it is your own or has a platform role (an admin removes the role first).

admin.title: Suspensions
admin.intro: Every suspension with who suspended, lifted and decided the appeal. Any moderator may suspend and decide appeals, so this list keeps the overview.

access.title: Access to the content
access.notTaken: Nobody has taken this case yet.
access.intro: Without access you see the reports and the title only. Access shows a read-only copy of this content for 24 hours; it is recorded with your reason, and admins can see it. The team is not notified.
access.reasonHint: Why do you need to see the content? Recorded and visible to admins; at most 500 characters.
access.takeFirst: Take the case first to open its content.
access.notice: Read-only access until {{end}}. Every view is recorded.

admin.title: Moderator accesses
admin.intro: Every access of a moderator to reported content, with the reason and the number of views.

statistics.title: Moderation statistics
statistics.intro: Sums per calendar month (UTC) for the last 12 months. No single cases or people.
statistics.breakdown: Reports by reason and by kind
statistics.note: Months without reports are left out of this table. Reports count in the month they were sent; decisions in the month they were made.

passwordChange.title: Password
passwordChange.wrongPassword: The current password is not correct.
passwordChange.weakPassword: The new password does not meet the rules: at least 12 characters, not a common password and not similar to your name or email address.

metrics.title: Growth metrics
metrics.intro: The five measures of success from the metrics concept, computed from the platform's own data. Counts, shares and medians only; never single people.
metrics.basis: Based on {{campaigns}} published campaigns, {{testers}} testers and {{developers}} publishing accounts.
metrics.privacy: No tracking: no page views, visits or click paths are recorded. Deleted accounts drop out. Months are calendar months in UTC.

explain.firstTester: Median time from publishing a campaign to its first participant (direct joining, accepted invitation or approved application; removed participants do not count). Campaigns without a participant appear in "Without a tester so far".
explain.completion: Completed campaigns divided by ended ones (completed or cancelled). Running campaigns do not count yet; teams close campaigns by hand.
explain.usefulFeedback: Share of completed campaigns with at least one feedback that was not marked as duplicate, cannot reproduce or rejected. Unprocessed feedback counts as useful.
explain.returningTesters: Share of people who took part in at least two campaigns, by the month of their first participation. Left participations count, removed ones do not.
explain.returningDevelopers: Share of accounts that published at least two campaigns, by the month of their first publication. The account that pressed "Publish" counts.
